title: Hold your ground and take the charge
description:
Start with the fall, ideally on a mat. In pairs: the defender stands in a stance and the attacker walks forward calmly with the ball held to the chest and gives a light bump. The defender sits backwards – seat on the floor first, then the back rolls down – with the chin on the chest and the arms in front of the body. No hands reaching back to the floor and no head hitting the floor.

Step two: the attacker dribbles at walking pace from the wing to the basket and the defender slides over from help to a spot in the attacker's path, outside the restricted area under the basket. The feet must be set and the chest square to the attacker before the contact. Step three: the same at jogging pace, and finally at game speed with the help coming from the weak side. Switch roles after every attempt.

Only move to the next step when everyone falls safely. In the drill the attacker must never jump or run straight into the defender. The diagram is not to scale.

coachingPoints.text: Get there in time: feet set, chest square to the attacker, outside the restricted area.
Take the contact on your chest – not with your hip, your arms or by sliding in at the last moment.
Fall safely: sit back, chin on chest and roll – hands stay in front of the body.
Get up quickly and back into the play if no call is made.

frames.note: Falling technique in pairs: A and B walk calmly forward with the ball and give a light bump, X and Y sit back with the chin on the chest and roll down.
Walking pace: A dribbles slowly to the basket. X slides over from help and sets up in A's path with the feet still, outside the restricted area.
Game speed: A drives to the basket and X rotates over from the weak side, gets the feet set and takes the charge.
